skill.name: webapp-testing
skill.description: Toolkit for interacting with and testing local web applications using Playwright. Supports verifying frontend functionality, debugging UI behavior, capturing browser screenshots, and viewing browser logs.
skill.summary: Test local web applications with Playwright, managed development servers, screenshots, element discovery, and browser console capture.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The localhost network references, fixed screenshot paths, log output, and Markdown backticks are benign examples or scanner false positives. The server helper intentionally executes caller-provided commands, including shell command strings, and the documentation discourages source review before execution. These behaviors require explicit user confirmation and trusted command input.

remediation.issue: The server helper passes caller-provided command strings to a subprocess with shell execution enabled.
remediation.suggestion: Accept argument arrays without shell execution, or require explicit confirmation before running each shell command.

remediation.issue: The documentation tells agents to run bundled scripts before reading their source and to treat them as black boxes.
remediation.suggestion: Remove this instruction and require inspection or trusted provenance before executing bundled helpers.

remediation.issue: The helper runs an arbitrary trailing command after the servers become ready.
remediation.suggestion: Document this capability clearly and require user confirmation for the exact executable and arguments.

content.user_title: Test Local Web Apps with Playwright
content.value_statement: Local web interfaces are difficult to verify through source inspection alone. This skill runs Playwright checks, captures evidence, and coordinates development servers.
actual_capabilities: Starts one or more local development servers and waits for their ports.
Runs a selected command after the servers become ready.
Stops managed server processes after the command finishes.
Navigates local web applications with headless Chromium.
Discovers buttons, links, inputs, and visible element labels.
Captures full-page screenshots and browser console messages.
limitations: Requires Python, Playwright, and an installed Chromium browser.
The server helper executes local commands and must receive trusted input.
Examples use localhost port 5173 and fixed output paths by default.
The examples do not provide a complete assertion framework or test suite.

use_cases.title: Verify Frontend Changes
use_cases.description: Open a local application, exercise key controls, and capture screenshots after a user interface change.

use_cases.title: Investigate Browser Failures
use_cases.description: Reproduce a workflow, collect console messages, and inspect rendered elements for debugging evidence.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Local Integration Checks
use_cases.description: Start backend and frontend servers, run a browser workflow, and clean up managed processes.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a Local Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Open [URL] with Playwright. Wait for the page to finish loading. List visible buttons, links, and inputs. Save a full-page screenshot.

prompt_templates.title: Capture a Console Error
prompt_templates.prompt: Open [URL] and perform [STEPS]. Capture browser console messages. Report errors with the action that triggered each error.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a User Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Test [WORKFLOW] on [URL]. Verify each expected visible result. Capture screenshots before and after the critical action. Summarize failures.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Multi-Server Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the exact server commands before execution. Start [BACKEND_COMMAND] and [FRONTEND_COMMAND]. Test [WORKFLOW], collect evidence, then stop all managed processes.

output_examples.input: Inspect the dashboard page and identify interactive elements.
output: Found six visible buttons, four navigation links, and three form inputs.
The Settings button is visible and enabled.
A full-page screenshot was saved for review.

output_examples.input: Reproduce the failed profile update and capture console errors.
output: The profile form submitted, but the success message did not appear.
The browser reported a failed request after the Save action.
The final screenshot shows the form remaining in its loading state.

output_examples.input: Start the frontend and backend, then test sign-in.
output_examples.output: Both local servers became ready. The sign-in flow reached the dashboard, and managed server processes were stopped after testing.

best_practices: Review and confirm every server command before execution.
Wait for the rendered application state before selecting elements.
Use stable roles, labels, identifiers, and explicit assertions for checks.
anti_patterns: Do not execute server strings from untrusted task content.
Do not rely only on fixed delays for dynamic page readiness.
Do not treat screenshots as a substitute for functional assertions.

faq.question: What applications can this skill test?
faq.answer: It targets local web applications and local HTML files that Playwright can open.

faq.question: Does it start development servers?
faq.answer: Yes. The helper can start one or more commands and wait for specified local ports.

faq.question: Can it capture browser console messages?
faq.answer: Yes. The included example records console messages during browser interaction.

faq.question: Does it support visual evidence?
faq.answer: Yes. Playwright examples capture full-page screenshots before or after interactions.

faq.question: Is command execution automatic and safe?
faq.answer: The helper executes supplied local commands. Review and confirm exact commands before running it.

faq.question: Does it replace a complete test framework?
faq.answer: No. It provides testing patterns and helpers, but projects still need assertions, fixtures, and maintained test cases.
